html:
Idrija is a town in western Slovenia where mercury was found in 1490, and its mine became the second largest source of mercury in the world after Almadén in Spain.

The Habsburgs took the mine over in 1575. Mercury was needed to refine silver by amalgamation, so Idrija's output reached the silver mines of Spanish America, and it was among the most profitable assets of the crown. Miners worked under hard conditions and many suffered mercury poisoning. The town also became known for bobbin lace, made by miners' wives. The mine closed in 1995 and is now a World Heritage Site, listed with Almadén.
sum: Idrija is a town in western Slovenia where mercury was found in 1490, and its mine became the second largest source of mercury in the world after Almadén in Spain.
